## Things to know about Marbella

### Exciting holiday in Marbella - Discover Andalusia

Discover the beautiful city of Marbella in [Andalusia](https://www.holidu.com/vacation-rentals/spain/andalusia), in the south of [Spain](https://www.holidu.com/vacation-rentals/spain). The metropolis of 140,000 inhabitants is located in the province of Málaga on the **Costa des Sol**. Marbella impresses with its splendid coastline and **beautiful beaches**. The city's coastline stretches for about 26 kilometres along the sea. Whether as a single person, as a couple or with the whole family - spend a varied holiday in a first-class holiday apartment in Marbella, Spain. Both in summer and in winter, the Andalusian holiday resort is a **popular sun destination**. Temperatures thus reach the 20 degree mark even in the winter months. Marbella is characterized by its **romantic old town**, its traditional street restaurants,

and the **exclusive marina Puerto Banús**. The hinterland of the province of Málaga is particularly beautiful, with its **unique mountain ranges** and **green river landscapes**. Let yourself be pampered by the delicious Spanish cuisine and try some original paella and sangria. The **high-quality infrastructure** on site, as well as the good service companies ensure that Marbella is an important and popular holiday destination. You can use public transport on site. * * *

Whether for a family, two families, or a larger group of friends, Villa Marbella offers ample space for up to 10 people, making it ideal for a dream holiday or as a second home during the winter, thanks to the long-term rental option.

The house, renovated in 2022, is surrounded by spacious south-facing terraces, perfect for relaxing on one of the sun loungers by the pool or on the inflatable beanbags, or for unwinding with yoga.

The terraces feature a freshwater pool and a summer kitchen equipped with a barbecue and fireplace.

The villa's orientation guarantees privacy and offers an unforgettable view of the Costa Adeje bay, a landscape that will captivate you all day and is sure to be the first image you will want to share with your loved ones.

Villa Marbella is centrally located, allowing you to enjoy both privacy and tranquility as well as easy access to the main attractions of the area, according to your preference.

It is an ideal base for exploring the island, visiting nearby beaches, or enjoying the lively local nightlife.

Guests especially appreciate the villa's location, the proximity to a supermarket, the possibility of parking if you rent a car or motorbike, and the fully equipped amenities for everyday life.

The villa offers comfort and options at any time of year and in any weather.

PARTIES ARE NOT ALLOWED.

## Luxury Villas, Cottages & Apartments in Marbella

### Book the Perfect Luxury Accommodation in Marbella

#### Why Rent a Luxury Villa, Cottage or Apartment in Marbella?

Marbella is a sun-soaked city where golden beaches, stylish marinas and charming historic streets come together in a vibrant Mediterranean setting. Visitors staying in a **luxury villa, cottage or apartment in Marbella** can wander through the Old Town with its cobbled lanes, whitewashed buildings and colourful flower-filled balconies or relax along the coastline where gentle waves meet sandy shores. The city offers a mix of high-end shopping, lively cafés and restaurants serving fresh seafood and Andalusian cuisine. Parks, promenades and quiet squares provide calm spots amid the energetic atmosphere. With a blend of culture, history and seaside charm, Marbella invites travellers to explore, unwind and savour the warmth of southern Spain.

For a change of scene, you might want to explore [luxury rentals in Marbella Centre](https://www.holidu.co.uk/f/luxury-rentals-marbella-centre-spain) to experience the bustling city centre with easy access to the Old Town and beaches. Alternatively, check out [villas in Málaga (Este)](https://www.holidu.co.uk/f/villas-malaga-este-spain) for a more relaxed coastal atmosphere with palm-lined walkways and traditional Andalusian charm.

#### What Are the Luxury Villas, Cottages & Apartments in Marbella Like?

Luxury villas, cottages and apartments in Marbella typically showcase modern designs combined with traditional Andalusian influences. These accommodations feature spacious interiors, elegant decor, and large outdoor areas perfect for entertaining. Many properties boast private pools, gardens, and terraces with stunning sea or mountain views. You can find these luxury rentals mainly in Marbella Centre, Costa del Sol, and the surrounding coastal areas. Some of the villas even come equipped with private pools, ideal for families or groups seeking exclusivity and comfort during their stay.

If you prefer a different style, you might also consider [villas in Benalmadena](https://www.holidu.co.uk/f/villas-benalmadena-spain), where the properties offer a mix of traditional charm and coastal views, perfect for a tranquil getaway.

Luxury rentals in Marbella often provide a wide range of amenities to ensure a comfortable and convenient stay:

- Private parking
- Air conditioning
- Wi-Fi
- Flat-screen TV
- Ocean views
- Gardens and/or private pools
- Barbecue facilities

## Travellers Who Would Enjoy Luxury Villas, Cottages & Apartments in Marbella

### Travellers and Activities

#### Marbella for Families

Families in Marbella can enjoy a mix of relaxed activities and cultural experiences that appeal to all ages. Parks and playgrounds provide safe spaces for children to run, climb and explore while parents relax on benches or stroll along shaded paths. The Old Town offers quiet streets, colourful plazas and small cafés perfect for family stops. Boat trips from the marina allow kids to spot dolphins, watch fishing boats and enjoy gentle sea breezes. Interactive museums and local craft workshops give young visitors hands-on experiences while learning about Andalusian culture. Even short walks along scenic promenades reveal fountains, street performers and hidden corners to discover! Be sure to browse the stunning selection of villas in Marbella Centre. Families might also like to check out [villas in Nerja](https://www.holidu.co.uk/f/villas-nerja-spain), as Nerja boasts clear turquoise waters, sandy coves and attractions such as the Nerja Caves, perfect for leisurely explorations and relaxation.

#### Marbella for Beach Lovers

Beach lovers in Marbella can explore long stretches of sand at Playa de la Fontanilla, Playa Nagüeles and the golden curve of Playa de Cabopino, where the water shifts from pale turquoise to deeper blue throughout the day. Gentle waves at Playa del Faro make it ideal for swimming and paddleboarding, while the dunes near Artola offer quieter corners for relaxed afternoons. Wooden boardwalks link the coast to chiringuitos such as Bono Beach and Restaurante Pekado Mortal, as well as lookout spots along the Paseo Marítimo where sunsets paint the sea in warm colours. Let the coastline become your playground and sanctuary all at once. Marbella's coastal charm and culinary delights offer endless opportunities to unwind, explore and soak in the sun. Those interested in seaside living might also consider exploring [villas in Marbella Centre](https://www.holidu.co.uk/f/villas-marbella-centre-spain) for easy access to beaches and waterfront activities.

> Did you know Marbella has hosted the prestigious Starlite Festival, the largest charity music festival in Europe, attracting global stars every summer?

### Top 7 Travel Tips in Marbella

#### 1\. Stroll Through the Old Town

Marbella's Old Town features narrow cobbled streets, whitewashed buildings and colourful flower-filled balconies. Walking through plazas, alleys and hidden squares reveals churches, fountains and artisan shops. Observation encourages photography, curiosity and appreciation of architectural details. Every corner tells stories of history, trade and local craftsmanship. Exploring the Old Town combines sensory engagement, learning and connection with culture. Hidden lanes uncover terraces, small gardens and tranquil squares. Streets immerse visitors in tradition, charm and enduring heritage. Walking through the Old Town reveals rhythm, colour and the character of Marbella.

#### 2\. Explore Golden Beaches and Seaside Promenades

Marbella offers wide golden beaches and calm waters, with stretches like Playa de la Fontanilla, Playa del Faro and Playa Nagüeles ideal for walking, sunbathing and swimming. Observing the shoreline reveals ripples in the sand, gentle waves at Playa de Venus and sunlight reflecting across the bay at Playa de la Bajadilla. Each beach has its own atmosphere, from the lively chiringuitos along Playa de Puerto Banús to the quieter dunes and inlets near Playa de Cabopino. Coastal promenades link these beaches with small parks, gardens and scenic viewpoints along the Paseo Marítimo. Walking the coastline blends movement with fresh sea air and constant engagement with the landscape.

#### 3\. Sample Local Cuisine and Tapas Bars

Restaurants, tapas bars and markets in Marbella serve classics such as espeto de sardinas grilled over open coals, boquerones en vinagre, salmorejo and Iberian ham carved to order. Many places offer seafood paella, pescaíto frito and gambas al pil-pil prepared with garlic and local olive oil. Tasting these dishes brings out the aromas of fresh herbs, citrus and Andalusian spices that define the region's cuisine. Markets like Mercado Municipal de Marbella showcase seasonal tomatoes, figs, olives and artisan cheeses alongside traditional pastries such as tortas de aceite. Dining here blends flavour, learning and a close connection to local cooking traditions.

#### 4\. Discover Luxury Marinas and Waterfront Life

Puerto Banús and smaller marinas feature yachts, colourful boats and lively cafés along the waterfront. Walking the quays allows observation of architectural style, bustling activity and marine details. Every corner offers photography opportunities, curiosity and sensory engagement. Exploring the marina combines movement, reflection and connection with coastal life. Paths reveal hidden shops, terraces and shaded benches. Each visit immerses visitors in luxury, charm and the rhythm of daily maritime activity. Waterfronts reveal contrasts, textures and the lively spirit of Marbella. The marina uncovers beauty, elegance and energy along the coast.

#### 5\. Hike Hills and Natural Parks

Trails through the Sierra Blanca and surrounding hills offer panoramic views of Marbella, coastline and inland landscapes. Observation reveals flora, rocky terrain and wildlife along the paths. Every trail provides exercise, reflection and moments for quiet appreciation. Paths wind through pine forests, valleys and ridges with lookout points and terraces. Hiking combines movement, sensory engagement and immersion in nature. Each summit immerses visitors in colour, light and dramatic scenery. Trails reveal textures, contrasts and the enduring energy of the hills. Exploring natural parks provides perspective, beauty and the charm of Marbella's inland landscapes.

#### 6\. Explore Artisan Markets and Boutiques

Markets, craft shops and local stores in Marbella showcase ceramics, handmade jewellery, embroidered textiles and Andalusian crafts. At the Puerto Banús Street Market, visitors can browse colourful pottery, leather bags and handwoven scarves, while the Marbella Old Town Market near Plaza de los Naranjos offers artisan soaps, olive-wood kitchenware and local honey. Small boutiques in the narrow streets of Casco Antiguo sell unique jewellery, painted tiles and locally made accessories. Walking through these stalls and shops reveals bright colours, traditional patterns and one-of-a-kind pieces!

#### 7\. Visit Cultural and Historical Landmarks

Marbella offers historic churches, palaces and monuments that reflect its long Andalusian past. Walking through the Casco Antiguo leads visitors to sites such as the Iglesia de la Encarnación, the Hermitage of Santiago and the 16th-century Town Hall with its carved stone façade. Around Plaza de los Naranjos, whitewashed houses and old arches reveal layers of civic and architectural history. Exploring places like the Museo del Grabado Español Contemporáneo or the remains of the Moorish castle walls provides insight into Marbella's cultural evolution. Narrow streets open onto hidden courtyards, small gardens and terraces overlooking tiled rooftops. Booking a luxury villa with a pool in Marbella is a must for the perfect holiday getaway.

## Marbella Holiday Rentals - come to the classic sunsoaked Spanish holiday jewel of the south coast

The city of Marbella is the second most populous municipality in the province of Malaga, after the homonymous provincial capital of Malaga, and the eighth most densely inhabited city of Andalusia, meaning it is the perfect holiday location for those on the hunt for an exciting, lively and action-packed city break with lots of people to meet. It is part of the popular coastal holiday region of Costa del Sol which is visited by thousands of tourists every year who flock to its shores from all over the world for the blissfully sunny weather, golden beaches, sparkling blue Mediterranean waters and gorgeous Marbella apartments. If hot and sunny weather, long stretches of idyllic beach, heavenly blue sea waters and wonderful holiday villas sound like your idea of holiday heaven, take a look at Begi Villas - where you can tour the Istrian vineyards and taste some of the world's most delicious wines!

## Marbella Holiday Villas - come and visit the sizzling Costa del Sol

There are 27 kilometres of idyllic coastline to explore in when renting **Marbella holiday homes**, divided into 24 separate beaches, the most notable being Artola, Venus and La Fontanilla, Puerto Banús and San Pedro Alcántara, which have been awarded the blue flag award for their clean water, safe surroundings and environmentally friendly practices, and Cabopino, one of the few nudist beaches in the city, for those who are feeling daring and adventurous! Marbella is undoubtedly one of the most important tourist city destinations on the Costa del Sol and attracts tourists to its shores all year round due to its favourable warm and pleasant climate and well-developed tourist infrastructure and facilities. The city also boasts an important not to be underestimated archaeological heritage, many fascianting history museums and a packed-out cultural calender, with a wide range of events to suit every possible taste, from reggae to opera, in the many concert and performance spaces located in the city.

## Marbella Villa Rentals - relax on the golden sandy beaches in the cool sea breeze

For those looking for a little history education on their Marbella holidays, head to the old town of Marbella, where you can spot the ancient city walls and the two historical suburbs of the city, namely, the Barrio Alto and the Barrio Nuevo, whose layout has remained practically untouched since the 16th century. Take a leisurely wander around the Plaza de los Naranjos, which was built after the Christian reconquest of the city, and see if you can spot some important buildings - the town hall, built in 1568 by the Catholic Monarchs the Mayor's house, with its Gothic and Renaissance façade, Mudejar roof and fresco murals in its interior, and the Chapel of Santiago, the oldest religious building in the city, which predates the square itself.
